correctness.rationale: Every strict cubic-nilpotent S of the target order has an intrinsic center and square {0,z}; all ternary products vanish, so its multiplication is an arbitrary two-valued binary table on r noncentral vertices. Prescribed graph constraints leave one bit per diagonal and unordered pair. Isomorphisms are precisely Aut(H) table relabelings. For an automorphism sigma, unordered-pair orbits contribute independent bits except a nonedge orbit with an endpoint swap; endpoint swaps arise exactly from even-cycle antipodal pairs. This proves the stated 0 or 2^(c+b) fixed-table law and Burnside count at all sizes. An exhaustive independent program checked 46 labeled eligible graphs through 4 vertices, and targeted counts through 6.

originality.rationale: Graph-conditioned isomorphism classes and the edge-dependent admissibility criterion are distinct from the previously published existence construction and order-aggregated class counts. The 2012 and 2024 papers already supply global table-orbit techniques; their coverage is explicitly credited. Conditionalizing on a prescribed commuting graph gives a new exact isomorphism-fiber count and a rigidity-all-realizations criterion, neither stated nor calculated in the inspected works. Priority outside the inspected corpus remains a risk.
residual_risks: Any prior exact graph-conditioned fiber or equivalent signed-table enumeration outside the inspected papers and searchable corpus could subsume the result.
Theorem is a graph-specific refinement of known power-group methods; the novelty is its edge-conditioned fixed-point and orbit classification, not the general Burnside or antipodal lemmas.

value.rationale: For every admissible graph H, the theorem solves a natural inverse classification problem: not just existence of an associative realization but the number of nonisomorphic minimal nilpotent realizations and whether any can have nontrivial automorphisms. The graph-dependent antipodal restriction and equal-fiber random-graph law are structural information unavailable from unrestricted order counts or a single realization. The infinite family and precise rigidity boundary make it relevant to semigroup and commuting-graph classification.
